programmes.d: Becker arrives at the office carrying the parking meter that ate his quarter.
Becker's patient, Jimmy, is a penniless scalper who is unable to afford his ulcer treatment.
On Jake's way out to meet his girlfriend, Becker warns him that his zipper is down.
Maya's tireless efforts for charity are overshadowed by her father's large cash donation.
Maya's experiment has unexpected consequences as Jack sets out to assemble a toy for his baby and Nina relishes her role in a practical joke on Finch.
While Maya finds it hard to fire an incompetent new assistant, Elliott and Finch conspire to embarrass Nina during a radio debate.
Maya and Jack square off over the advanced age of her new boyfriend; Nina's flirtatious behavior has unintended consequences for a handsome window washer.
Finch ignores all warnings and gets involved with Elliott's old girlfriend.
A request to get her father to stop his favoritism backfires and costs Maya a trip to London.
Maya's article about Woody Allen catches the eye of an impostor.
Jack must prove himself worthy in order to get his young daughter admitted to a prestigious private school.
Maya's efforts to do something nice for a janitor backfires.
Elliott vows to use a high school teacher's funeral to prove something to his old classmates.
Maya tries proving herself to a successful college roommate; Jack's birthday sets Finch and Nina to fighting over who can find the best present.
Finch must convince his dad that he isn't gay.
When Alan dates a cooking instructor, Sandy, both he and Charlie gain weight. Charlie refuses to allow Alan to break up with her, fearing the loss of her fabulous meals.
Charlie and Alan take Jake to a friend's house and go out for some sibling bonding, but Alan convinces himself that Jake was too eager to spend the weekend away from him.
No one believes Charlie when he says that his relationship with Mia is getting serious.
After a month and a half of abstinence, Charlie is quite eager to consummate his relationship with Mia. Unfortunately, there are still a few roadblocks.
Charlie's lifestyle causes tension with Mia. Charlie can't keep pace with the healthy routine that Mia has introduced, so he sneaks cigars and beers in the garage.
Concerned that he is dating a woman half his age--and mortified to introduce her to Evelyn--Alan tries to avoid bringing his 22-year-old girlfriend, Kandi, to Jake's birthday party.
When he is nominated for an advertising award, Charlie boycotts the banquet, having lost several years in a row to his cocky competitor, Archie.
Alan gets into financial trouble because he keeps paying the expenses of his young girlfriend, Kandi. When Kandi's old car breaks down, Alan leases a new one for her.
Kandi moves in with Alan and Charlie, causing tension in the house. Charlie's not happy to learn of the new arrangement, considering he has been having a dry spell with women.
Charlie is now dating Kandi's mother, Mandi. Meanwhile, Alan is depressed because Kandi has left him and is staying with bitter Judith, who brainwashed her against him.
Jake's teacher, Francine, calls Alan and Judith into her classroom to discuss Jake's lack of interest in school.
When a cute girl from Jake's school invites Jake to a party, Charlie butts in on Alan's milestone moment with his son by offering his own words of wisdom on women.
When Charlie finds out that his ex, Mia, is in town with her dance troupe and wants him to come to her performance, he tries to behave as if he were no longer attracted to her.
With Charlie and Mia arranging their wedding, their families meet, and things immediately begin to fall apart. Rose takes Charlie's engagement news hard.
In the season premiere, Charlie deals with the immediate aftermath of his canceled wedding—and Alan's impulsive new marriage to 22-year-old Kandi.
Alan feels guilty when Charlie finally tells him why he broke up with Mia. The truth is that Charlie and Mia didn't get married because she had wanted Alan and Jake to move out.

A down-on-his-luck shoe salesman, Al Bundy, who’s unhappily married with two children, is forced to choose between going to a basketball game or joining his lazy wife, Peg, in meeting their new neighbors.

Marcy introduces Peg to a new energetic diet to improve her marriage. Al, meanwhile, wants to part of it but learns if he tries the diet, he can persuade Peg to quit. He must then swallow his pride and admit to Peggy he loves her no matter what.

It's the Bundy’s 16th wedding anniversary. Al plans to buy Peggy a very fancy watch, but unfortunately, his credit card gets declined. Dare he show up at the party without a present?

There has been a rash of burglaries in the area, and the Rhodes' house is robbed and Al's car stereo is ripped off. Steve and Marcy buy a guard dog that won't stop barking, and Al purchases a fire arm. Ultimately, the two methods of home defense clash.
Al and Steve buy a beat up Ford Mustang off of one of Kelly's boyfriends. Soon they form a tight friendship while fixing it up like new. The only problem is they are neglecting their wives.
Steve and Marcy plan to add a new room onto their house using their tax refund money. Al convinces Steve to make it into a billiards room while Peggy convinces Marcy to make it into an exercise room.
Al gets a first-hand look at swinging bachelor life when he takes refuge at Luke's apartment after an argument with Peggy over visiting her relatives for the weekend.
To get the money to purchase a new VCR that Al won't buy her, Peggy takes a job in a department store selling clocks.
When Al and Peg decide to go on vacation, Steve and Marcy volunteer to take care of their kids, Bud and Kelly. But, their enthusiasm changes when the kids throw a huge party at the Rhoades' house.

Al invites Steve to play poker with his friends but ends up losing his paycheck to Al. Avoiding telling the truth to Marcy fails as Al plans to use his winnings to buy a fishing rod. Ultimately, Marcy enlists the help of Peggy to stop him.

When the owner of the shoe store is in a near-fatal plane crash, Al decides that it is time to get some recognition from his boss or quit his job. After quitting, Al returns to the shoe store, but not without a surprise.

Marcy freaks out when she begins having erotic dreams about Al after a heated argument about men vs women, and wonders whether she is actually sexually attracted to Al. Haunted by her dreams, Marcy ultimately comes to a conclusion and confronts Al.
Charlie attempts to surf in order to impress a beautiful girl—with disastrous results. After nearly drowning, he tells Alan that the guys' deceased father appeared to him.
Alan is determined to retain custody of his and Kandi's dog after Kandi walks away from their split with both the condominium and the car.
Alan is overjoyed that he'll no longer owe Judith alimony when she marries her new fiancé, Herb. However, Judith and Herb's marriage plans are threatened.
Although Charlie doesn't get along with his sharp-tongued, passive-aggressive mother, he is strangely attracted to Lydia, a blonde high-end real estate agent—what his mother is.
When Berta swears vengeance on the married man who got her daughter, Naomi, pregnant, she forces Charlie to come with her. Meanwhile, Naomi helps Berta with the housework.
